draft.title: Infrared spectroscopy
card: In infrared (IR) spectroscopy, a sample absorbs infrared light. Each type of bond vibrates and absorbs at its own range of wavenumber, measured in cm⁻¹.
The spectrum plots how much light passes through against wavenumber. Each absorption shows as a peak pointing down, so a peak means a bond of that type is present.

Useful peaks: a strong, sharp C=O peak at about 1700 cm⁻¹. A broad O-H peak from an alcohol at about 3200 to 3550 cm⁻¹. A very broad O-H peak from a carboxylic acid at about 2500 to 3300 cm⁻¹. An N-H peak at about 3300 to 3500 cm⁻¹.
Peaks are matched to a data table to find which functional groups are present. IR does not give the molar mass or the full structure.
draft.remember: Each bond absorbs at its own wavenumber, so peaks point to functional groups.

a.q: An IR spectrum of an unknown compound has a strong, sharp peak at about 1700 cm⁻¹. What does this show?
opts: The molar mass is about 1700 g/mol
a.why: A strong, sharp peak near 1700 cm⁻¹ is the absorption of a C=O bond. An O-H bond would give a broad peak at higher wavenumber. IR does not measure molar mass.
a.clue: Match the wavenumber to a bond in the data table.

b.q: An IR spectrum of a liquid has a strong peak at about 1700 cm⁻¹ and a very broad peak from about 2500 to 3300 cm⁻¹. Which compound fits best?
b.why: The C=O peak and the very broad O-H peak together show a carboxylic acid, so ethanoic acid fits. Propanone and ethyl ethanoate have C=O but no O-H. Ethanol has a broad O-H peak but no C=O peak.
b.clue: Which compound has both a C=O bond and an O-H bond?

problems.detail: The remember line says each bond absorbs at 'its own wavenumber', but the card correctly says 'its own range of wavenumber'. The remember line could suggest a single exact value.
The carboxylic acid O-H range is given as 2500 to 3300 cm⁻¹. Many textbooks use this, but the NSW HSC data sheet gives 2500–3000 cm⁻¹. Students using the data sheet may see a mismatch. This is minor.

check.summary: Both questions are correct, with clear single answers (C=O present; ethanoic acid). Two minor issues: the remember line drops 'range' from 'own range of wavenumber', and the acid O-H range differs slightly from the NSW data sheet's 2500–3000 cm⁻¹.
